new_packages.label: גַּדְלוּת הַמֹּחִין וְהַדַּעַת
new_packages.qualifies_because: Six bechina-connected concepts forming an independent thematic domain not covered by any existing package. These concepts share the essential nature of 'elevated/full consciousness and its divine attributes'. The bechina chain: da'at ↔ gadlut hamochin ↔ [El ↔ chesed] + [YHVH ↔ rachamim]. All six nodes are explicitly identified as bechinot of each other or of the central theme via the markers 'הוּא', 'נִקְרָא', and 'הַיְנוּ'.
new_packages.independence_argument: The domain of gadlut/da'at/divine-Names does not appear as a pre-existing package in the global dataset under this specific Torah (#106). While da'at and chesed/rachamim appear in other Torahs, Torah #106 creates a specific and local cluster where gadlut hamochin is THE central bechina of da'at, and the two Names (El and YHVH) are the specific bechinot of chesed and rachamim respectively. This local configuration, expressed in the context of this Torah's argument (ascending from katnut), constitutes an independent package.

new_packages.label: קַטְנוּת הַמֹּחִין וְהָעֲנִיּוּת
new_packages.qualifies_because: Four bechina-connected concepts forming an independent thematic domain — the evil/deficiency mirror of Package 106-A. These concepts share the essential nature of 'diminished consciousness / absence of da'at'. The bechina chain: aniyut ↔ chisaron da'at ↔ katnut hamochin ↔ dal. All four nodes are explicitly identified as bechinot via the markers 'אֵין...אֶלָּא' (exclusive identification = bechina), 'נִקְרָא', and 'הַיְנוּ'.
new_packages.independence_argument: The domain of katnut/aniyut is structurally independent from the gadlut domain — they are the two poles of the same axis. Katnut hamochin is the specific concept coined in this Torah (it is a technical term defined here: 'it is called katnut hamochin'). Its cluster of four nodes forms a coherent evil-polarity package that mirrors Package 106-A exactly.

observations:
Torah #106 is extremely short (8 lines) but structurally complete. It presents a pure binary: the human soul exists either in katnut (diminished consciousness = spiritual poverty = dal) or in gadlut (expanded consciousness = da'at = access to El/chesed and YHVH/rachamim). The two packages are the two poles of this binary.

Since the dataset contains ZERO bechina edges for Torah #106, BOTH packages are entirely new — not merges of existing data, but first-time extractions from the source text. The teaching requires 10 new nodes and approximately 10 new bechina edges to be added to the dataset before it can be represented in the graph.

The good/evil mirror structure is the clearest possible: one package is the positive pole, one is the negative pole, and they mirror each other concept-by-concept:
  - גדלות המוחין ↔ קטנות המוחין
  - דעת ↔ חסרון דעת
  - אל (El/chesed) — present under gadlut, absent under katnut
  - ה' (YHVH/rachamim) — present under gadlut, absent under katnut

The Torah's single eitza connection (edge 2279: enlightening others → one's own awakening) is the bridge between packages: it is the practical instruction (eitza) for moving from Package B (katnut) to Package A (gadlut). This is a textbook eitza-between-packages structure.

The verse 'beyom ra'ah yemalteihu YHVH — nimtakin kol hadinim' is the eitza outcome of reaching gadlut (Package A). It is not a bechina and belongs to the eitza layer of the Torah's argument, not to any package.
